Abstract mentions 'normal hemostatic function' but study includes patients with spinal deformity; however, no clear exclusion criteria. Upon re-review, it appears to be an RCT in surgical population. But note: the abstract does not mention comparison to placebo or active comparator? It says 'Seventeen patients were designated to receive 10 micrograms/m2 of desmopressin, and 18, to receive a placebo.' So it is placebo-controlled. Wait, I misread. Actually it is RCT with placebo. However, the population is patients with normal hemostatic function undergoing spinal fusion. This should be INCLUDE. Let me correct: This is an RCT, DDAVP vs placebo, in spinal fusion surgery. No inherited bleeding disorders. So INCLUDE.

Study population is cardiac surgical patients pretreated with aspirin (antiplatelet therapy) which may alter coagulation; however, not explicitly an inherited bleeding disorder. But the study compares DDAVP to saline placebo and measures blood requirements. This appears to be an RCT. Wait, the abstract says 'In a double-blind, randomized trial'... So it is an RCT. Why did I exclude? Because I thought it mentioned inherited bleeding disorders? It does not. It says 'patients preoperatively treated with platelet-inhibiting drugs' (aspirin). This is not an inherited bleeding disorder. So this should be INCLUDE. Let me re-evaluate: The study is an RCT, DDAVP vs placebo, in cardiac surgery (perioperative), measuring blood requirements. No inherited bleeding disorders. So INCLUDE.
